text: I'm designing a study to measure the prevalence of debt bondage in the PH-HK domestic-worker corridor. What sampling frame would give me defensible numbers (vs. obvious selection bias)? Discuss tradeoffs: surveying at the airport on return, partnering with an NGO shelter, snowball through Filipino community groups in HK, paid-recruitment via social-media ads. End with a concrete recommendation and the n you'd target.

Design a study that detects AI-generated recruitment ads at scale across TikTok / Facebook / Telegram. Discuss tradeoffs: (a) fingerprint generative-AI artifacts in images; (b) cluster ads by template variance; (c) crowdsource flagging from worker-side respondents; (d) regulatory partnership with TikTok / Meta. What's the n you'd target, what's the realistic detection precision, what's the publishable finding?

I'm writing a journal article on Saudi Arabia's domestic-worker recruitment market. I need: (1) the most-recent verified prevalence of debt bondage in the Saudi domestic-worker population (with measurement window + methodology); (2) the post-2021 Saudi Labour Reform Initiative's measured compliance impact; (3) the documented limitations of available data (self-report bias, undocumented-worker undercount). Cite primary sources, not secondary commentary.

I'm writing a methods section for a paper on trafficking-detection LLM evaluation. Walk through: (1) the G-Eval / MT-Bench / Auto-J methodology lineage; (2) the documented limitations of self-graded LLMs (positional bias, length bias, self-preference); (3) when frontier judges are warranted and when they're not; (4) the abliterated-model-as-judge tradeoff for adversarial-suite scoring; (5) inter-rater-agreement reporting standards (Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha) for LLM-as-judge studies.
